title: About ten rescuers missing after two boats capsize in flooded Khammam tank
dek: SDRF and fire service personnel were trying to reach fishermen trapped in Telangana's overflowing Bethupalli tank after Cyclone Murasu's rains. NDRF teams have been sent to join the search.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
About ten rescue workers went missing in Telangana's Khammam district on Wednesday evening when their two boats capsized in a flooded tank, where they had gone to rescue stranded fishermen. They were still missing when the last reports came in overnight, and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams were sent to join the search.

The boats went down in the overflowing Bethupalli tank, also called Peddacheruvu, in Sathupalli mandal, after heavy rain from Cyclone Murasu. Reports differ on the number missing: Deccan Chronicle and Telangana Today put it at 10 personnel of the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and Fire Services, UNI also said 10, and The Hindu said "around nine", including five SDRF personnel. Siasat and some other outlets reported 11. The state government had not published an official figure by the time of writing.

## What happened

Five fishermen went into the tank to set nets near its weir and were trapped when the water rose suddenly, Telangana Today reported; it said water was flowing about three feet over the spillway. Three Fire Services personnel set out by boat to reach them but were caught in the current, according to Deccan Chronicle.

Six SDRF personnel from Kothagudem and four more firefighters then went out in two boats. They brought the first three firefighters back safely and reached some of the fishermen, but both boats capsized as they went for the rest. Locals suspect the boats were caught in fishing nets, Telangana Today reported; UNI cited strong winds and currents. The Hindu reported that the five fishermen were said to be safe, while Telangana Today said three were still stranded when it reported on Wednesday night.

## The search

A second SDRF team from Bhadrachalam began a search, and divers and trained swimmers were brought in. Officials planned to use drones to drop life jackets, The Hindu reported. Bad weather and poor visibility hampered the work overnight.

Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy told officials to intensify the search and asked Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju to monitor it, Deccan Chronicle reported. Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy said he would visit the site on Thursday morning. Union Minister Bandi Sanjay Kumar said he had spoken to senior NDRF officials, and NDRF teams were sent to Sathupalli, according to The Hindu. District Collector Divakara TS and Sathupalli MLA Matta Ragamayi were at the site.

Agriculture Minister Tummala Nageswara Rao told officials to trace the mobile phone locations of the missing men, Deccan Chronicle reported.

Floodwater from the tank also flowed into the nearby Veshyakanthala tank and flooded a housing complex up to the first floor; residents were moved to relief centres, Telangana Today said.

## Background

Cyclone Murasu crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole early on 3 November as a severe cyclonic storm and moved inland, bringing extremely heavy rain to Khammam and Bhadradri Kothagudem districts of Telangana on 4 November, The Hindu reported.

We will update this story when officials confirm the number missing and the result of the search.
